subject: Evidence for VM controls: scan cadence, triage matrix, and SLA commitments
messages:
From: Elena Costa <elena@trustassure.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: vulnerability management evidence for SIG/CAIQ audit

Hi Jonas,

FinSecure's security team is running a SIG/CAIQ review and requested additional evidence around Redwood's vulnerability management program. Could you provide the following artifacts and clarifications by end of week?

- Confirmation of active scan cadence (authenticated/cloud-agent vs unauthenticated) and retention of scan results.
- SLA targets for CVE remediation by severity and how exceptions are handled.
- A sample of the triage matrix/process that maps CVE risk to action (patch, mitigate, accept) and owners.
- Examples of evidence used for SOC 2/third-party reviews (commit links, patch tickets, exception approvals).

Files can be redacted for PII. If you have a short cover note summarizing the program and the most recent scan index, that would be ideal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if it's easier.

Best,
Elena Costa
TrustAssure — Senior Audit Manager
elena@trustassure.com
+1 415 555 0193

Attachment requested: latest scan index, remediation status export

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Costa <elena@trustassure.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Mar 2028 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management evidence for SIG/CAIQ audit

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (security/compliance) and Marissa (infrastructure ops) who maintain the scan schedule and remediation trackers. Below is a concise summary; attached are the artifacts you asked for.

Summary (high level)
- Scan cadence:
  - Authenticated dynamic scans against runtime fabric: weekly (every Wed, 02:00 UTC).
  - Full network/host scans (agent-based) for dedicated/private deployments: bi-weekly.
  - SBOM & dependency vulnerability scans (SCA): daily for published artifacts; monthly for infra images.
  - Retention: raw scan results kept for 13 months; aggregated indices & trend data retained for 3 years.

- CVE remediation SLAs (target windows from detection to remediation or documented exception):
  - Critical (CVSS 9.0–10.0 or exploit observed): remediation or mitigated workaround within 7 business days.
  - High (CVSS 7.0–8.9): remediation or mitigated workaround within 14 calendar days.
  - Medium (CVSS 4.0–6.9): remediation planned within 60 calendar days; tracked in backlog.
  - Low (<4.0): prioritized by business impact; typical horizon 180 days.

- Exception process: documented exceptions require a formal risk acceptance ticket (owner, compensating controls, expiry), approval from the product/security owner, and quarterly review. Exceptions are treated as a change and tracked in our audit log.

- Triage matrix & ownership: attached CSV maps CVSS + asset criticality to action (patch, isolate, config-change, accept) and primary owners (Infra Eng, Runtime SRE, Platform Security).

Attachments included: redwood-vm-scan-index-20280308.pdf (summary index), cve-remediation-matrix-20280308.csv (triage matrix + backlog snapshot), scan-schedule-snapshot-20280308.txt (cron schedule export). Also included sample links (in sample-remediation-evidence-urls.txt) showing commit hashes and ticket IDs we supply during audits.

If you need raw scan exports instead of the PDF index we can produce them under an encrypted transfer. Let us know which items you want redacted.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Costa <elena@trustassure.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: FinSecure Audit Team <audit@finsecure.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management evidence for SIG/CAIQ audit

Jonas — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of clarifying questions before we escalate to our audit panel:

1) For the 7-business-day SLA on Criticals — do you have evidence of adherence over the last 12 months (e.g., % closed within SLA, a sample of critical CVE tickets)?
2) Does "mitigated workaround" require a code patch, or can it be a configuration change / network ACL as long as it's tracked and time-boxed?
3) For private/dedicated deployments, who owns patching vs the customer? Any standard carve-outs we should document?

If you can provide a small sample (3–5 tickets/commit links) demonstrating closure within the SLA and a one-paragraph definition for what qualifies as "remediated" vs "mitigated," that will likely close most of our panel's items.

Thanks — we aim to finalize our notes Monday.

—Elena

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Costa <elena@trustassure.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: vulnerability management evidence for SIG/CAIQ audit

Elena — quick follow-up with the specific items you requested. Per Marissa's export (attached sample-remediation-evidence-urls.txt) we've included 4 anonymized ticket links showing critical CVE handling across the last 12 months; each entry includes: detection timestamp, ticket ID, owner, remediation action, and closure timestamp. Summary stats: of 12 critical findings in the last 12 months, 11 were resolved within the 7-business-day target; the single miss was due to an upstream vendor patch delay and is annotated with exception approval.

Definition: "Remediated" = code or configuration change that eliminates the vulnerable condition (e.g., patched dependency, config change removing vulnerable capability) and is validated by a successful follow-up scan or test. "Mitigated" = compensating control that reduces exploitability (network ACL, feature flag, runtime guard) with a documented timeline and owner; requires a follow-up remediation plan. Both require a ticket, owner, and verification evidence to be considered compliant for SOC 2 purposes.

Private/Dedicated carve-outs: we operate under a shared-responsibility model. For hosted Redwood-managed infra we own patching and remediation. For customer-managed private nodes (on-prem or customer VPC with customer-managed images), we provide vulnerability findings and recommended fixes; remediation is the customer's responsibility unless otherwise contracted (see section 3.2 of the DPA). We included a one-page excerpt in the PDF index.

Next steps:
- I attached the requested samples and the triage matrix.
- If FinSecure needs raw scan artifacts or audit-signed attestations, we can schedule a secure transfer and a short walkthrough with our SREs.

Let us know if that covers everything for your panel.

Regards,
Jonas
